adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the hypothesis's own cited predictable case: half after second should stay near zero despite being a claimed trigger token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Where are you going after school today?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the cited predictable case: are after Where should stay near zero despite are being a claimed trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I am happy to see you again today.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger token am in a highly predictable context (I am), which the hypothesis predicts should not spike.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: So far so good, the project is on track.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger token far in a frozen idiom (so far) where far is strongly predicted by so, predicting no spike.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The toddler counted one two three out loud.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger token three in a counting sequence where it is fully predicted by two, predicting no spike.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Please open your textbook to Chapter 1 now.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger token 1 in a predictable context (Chapter 1) rather than after equals, predicting no spike.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Once upon a time there was a sleepy dragon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same-topic words as example 1 but a frozen collocation (Once upon) where upon is fully predictable, predicting no spike.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: New York City never sleeps at night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Highly predictable multiword continuation (New York) with no weakly-predicted token, predicting no spike.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She laughed and said ha ha that is funny.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Exact token repetition (ha ha) is maximally predictable, so the hypothesis predicts the repeated token stays near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Enter your password and press enter to log in.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic as example 8 (password) but only routine predictable instructions with no surprising continuation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: SELECT name FROM users ORDER BY name ASC;
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic and vocabulary as example 2 (SQL) but only canonical predictable keywords with no surprising literal.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She ironed the soup before folding the laundry.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel surprising direct-object continuation (ironed the soup) that is weakly predicted by the preceding token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lighthouse sang purple during the midnight storm.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre poetic holdout with a weakly predicted verb complement (sang purple) unlike any example.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee voted to elect the refrigerator as chair.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel surprising noun (elect the refrigerator) after a strongly constraining verb frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After filing taxes, he celebrated by baptizing his dentist.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel surprising possessed noun (his dentist) after a verb frame predicting a different argument; single-token surprise unlike the split lawnmower.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The quantum textbook proved that Tuesday smells like copper.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre surprising predicate (Tuesday smells) violating a strong day-of-week prediction.
